title: Semantic Law Matrix — digital consumer law
method: Classification vectors over normative primitives; cosine geometry, agglomerative clustering and SVD embedding computed in Wolfram Language, re-derived in Python and cross-checked before publication.
disclaimer: Analyst scaffold current to 2026-08. A research instrument, not legal advice; re-check each row against primary sources before relying on it.

primitives.label: Consent
primitives.gloss: A freely given, specific act of permission is the gate to the conduct.

primitives.label: Transparency
primitives.gloss: Mandated disclosure of terms, identity, ranking, or provenance.

primitives.label: Substantive fairness
primitives.gloss: The balance of the bargain is policed, not merely its disclosure.

primitives.label: Exit and withdrawal
primitives.gloss: The consumer may leave: cancel, withdraw, unsubscribe, port out.

primitives.label: Redress
primitives.gloss: A remedy runs to the individual: repair, refund, damages, restitution.

primitives.label: Liability allocation
primitives.gloss: The rule fixes who bears loss when the digital thing fails.

primitives.label: Enforcement severity
primitives.gloss: Turnover-based fines, injunctions, or personal liability attach.

primitives.label: Extraterritorial reach
primitives.gloss: The rule binds suppliers established outside the forum.

primitives.label: Vulnerable users
primitives.gloss: Heightened duties toward minors, the elderly, the distressed.

primitives.label: Data minimisation
primitives.gloss: Purpose limitation and necessity constrain collection.

primitives.label: Interoperability
primitives.gloss: Portability, open interfaces, switching without loss.

primitives.label: Auditability
primitives.gloss: Records, reporting, audits, or researcher access are compelled.

primitives.label: Timeliness
primitives.gloss: Hard deadlines govern acting, responding, or notifying.

primitives.label: Security duty
primitives.gloss: A technical protection standard is imposed on the supplier.

primitives.label: Per se prohibition
primitives.gloss: Conduct is banned outright, no balancing available.

primitives.label: Ex ante structure
primitives.gloss: Compliance is designed in before launch, not litigated after.

gaps.label: Conformity of digital content and services

classes.label: General data protection
classes.verify: Confirm lawful-basis architecture and the current adequacy/transfer position for each forum.

classes.label: Cookies, trackers and communications confidentiality
classes.verify: ePrivacy remains a directive with divergent national consent rules; check the member-state rule, not the directive alone.

classes.label: Profiling and behavioural advertising
classes.verify: Sensitive-category and minors advertising bans differ sharply; verify per platform tier.

classes.label: Data portability and interoperability
classes.verify: Data Act obligations phase in over time; confirm the applicable date and product scope.

classes.label: Automated decision-making and consumer AI
classes.verify: AI Act duties phase in by risk tier; check which obligations are in force on the relevant date.

classes.label: Unfair contract terms
classes.verify: Australia moved to penalties for unfair terms in 2023; confirm the penalty exposure, not just voidness.

classes.label: Distance selling and pre-contractual information
classes.verify: Information duties are itemised and jurisdiction-specific; compare item lists rather than assuming equivalence.

classes.label: Cooling-off and right of withdrawal
classes.verify: Digital-content withdrawal is lost on performance with consent; verify how that waiver is captured.

classes.label: Auto-renewal and cancellation
classes.verify: The FTC click-to-cancel rule has been litigated; confirm its status and effective date before relying on it.

classes.label: Price transparency and drip pricing
instruments: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees
classes.verify: Junk-fee rules differ on whether taxes and shipping enter the headline price.

classes.label: Personalised and algorithmic pricing
classes.verify: Thin and mostly disclosure-based; surveillance-pricing enforcement is developing, so re-check activity.

classes.label: Conformity of digital content and services
classes.verify: Objective conformity plus the update duty is an EU/UK construct; elsewhere it is general warranty law.

classes.label: Goods with digital elements
classes.verify: The CRA's obligations are phased; confirm which apply on the relevant date.

neighbours.label: Conformity of digital content and services

classes.label: Update duty, repair and obsolescence
classes.verify: Support-period lengths and parts-availability duties vary by product category.

classes.label: Liability for defective digital products
classes.verify: The recast PLD brings software and AI into strict liability; confirm transposition status.

classes.label: Consumer IoT and product cybersecurity
classes.verify: Default-password and vulnerability-disclosure duties are the common core; certification schemes differ.

classes.label: Marketplace and ranking transparency
classes.verify: Trader-identity (KYBC) duties apply only to marketplaces; check the service classification first.

classes.label: Intermediary liability and notice-and-action
classes.verify: The US safe harbour and the EU due-diligence model point in opposite directions; do not merge them.

classes.label: Gatekeeper and digital-markets duties
classes.verify: Designation is entity-specific; confirm whether the counterparty is actually designated.

classes.label: User rights in content moderation
instruments: DSA arts.14-21 (statement of reasons, internal appeal, out-of-court settlement)
classes.verify: Appeal and out-of-court dispute rights are largely an EU innovation; check local analogues carefully.

classes.label: Illegal and harmful content duties
classes.verify: Risk-assessment and age-assurance duties turn on service size and type.

classes.label: Misleading and aggressive practices
classes.verify: The nearest thing to a universal rule in this field; the blacklist contents still differ.

classes.label: Manipulative interface design
instruments: CPRA s.1798.140(h) (consent obtained by dark pattern is not consent)
classes.verify: Mostly enforced through existing unfairness law; only the DSA and CPRA name the conduct directly.

classes.label: Fake reviews and undisclosed endorsements
instruments: FTC Rule on Consumer Reviews and Testimonials 2024
classes.verify: Verification duties (did the reviewer buy it?) are stronger than mere prohibition; check which applies.

classes.label: Unsolicited marketing and spam
classes.verify: Opt-in versus opt-out is the fault line: CASL and ePrivacy are opt-in, CAN-SPAM is opt-out.

classes.label: Children, minors and age assurance
classes.verify: Age thresholds and assurance standards diverge; a compliant flow in one forum can be unlawful in another.

classes.label: Accessibility of digital services
classes.verify: The EAA applies from June 2025 with micro-enterprise carve-outs; confirm the entity size test.

classes.label: Electronic payments and unauthorised transactions
classes.verify: Liability-shift rules for unauthorised transactions differ in both cap and burden of proof.

classes.label: Crypto-asset consumer protection
classes.verify: Promotion rules and custody duties are moving fast; treat any score here as provisional.

classes.label: Digital credit and buy-now-pay-later
classes.verify: CCD2 applies from Nov 2026; confirm whether the transition rules cover the transaction.

classes.label: Collective redress and dispute resolution
classes.verify: The EU ODR platform was wound down in 2025; do not cite it as a live route.

classes.label: Cross-border enforcement and cooperation
classes.verify: Cooperation instruments give regulators reach that private claimants do not have.

divergence.label: Conformity of digital content and services
